title: U.S. used 'virtually all' of its long-range precision missiles during Iran war
titleZh: 美国在伊朗战争期间使用了“几乎所有”远程精确导弹
author: tcp_handshaker
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: The U.S. Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during its five-month war with Iran, according to three people familiar ⁠with the data, raising concerns about the military's readiness for future conflicts.The missiles are principally the Army's surface-to-surface weapons, known as Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM). The U.S. has used "virtually all" of these weapons, according to two of the sources.The degree to which the ​military is running out of ATACMS and Precision Strike Missiles has not ​been previously reported. The long-range munitions are an important part ​the military's arsenal, allowing accurate strikes from a safe distance. U.S.-supplied ATACMS have played a key role in the war in Ukraine, allowing Ukrainian forces to attack targets inside Russia. The PrSM is a newer, more advanced generation that will replace the ATACMS, which have a shorter range.Analysts say such weapons – which cost over $1 million each – would also be important in any conflict with China.The sources declined to say how many of each munition the U.S. had left.President Donald Trump launched the ⁠Iran war ‌jointly with Israel in February, predicting that the conflict would last a short time.But as the war drags on, the ⁠three people familiar with the matter expressed worry that the falling missile supplies could limit the U.S. ability to deter adversaries, including Russia and China.A fourth person familiar with the matter said that while Central Command — which oversees U.S. forces in the Middle East — has nearly used up the land-based missiles it had before the war began, it has been able to reload from U.S. military supplies elsewhere in the world.The sources interviewed for this story spoke on the condition of anonymity.Asked for comment on the stockpile data, the White House issued a statement ‌from Trump, saying the U.S. had "far more munitions than anyone in the world" and "far more than we need.""Our defense companies are, at this moment, making more munitions than they have ever made before, in addition to expanding their plants and equipment at record levels," Trump said.Analysts agree that certain munitions, including artillery shells and several types of missiles, are being produced at record levels but caution that ​supplies might far short of what is needed for a prolonged war.Lockheed Martin, which makes the ATACMs and PrSMs, along with the anti-ballistic missile THAAD system, did not immediately respond to questions about Trump's statements or about supply levels. Raytheon, which makes Tomahawk missiles and Patriot interceptors, two important U.S. weapons, also did not immediately respond.Responding to a request for comment, chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said: "America's military is the most powerful in the world and has everything it needs to execute at the time and place of the President's choosing. We have executed multiple successful operations across combatant commands while ensuring the U.S. military possesses a ⁠deep arsenal of capabilities to protect our people and our interests."The supply figures have circulated inside the federal government over the last week during tense conversations inside the Trump administration about how much longer the U.S. can continue striking Iran without drawing down the ‌stockpile to levels that would limit the military's ability to respond to crises elsewhere.Warnings over weapons supplies One of the sources said the drawdown of the ‌ATACMS and PrSM stockpiles reflected a decision by the Trump administration to avoid riskier ways of attacking Iranian targets, such as by using piloted aircraft to drop bombs.Because these weapons allow the military to attack targets from a distance, analysts say they would be valuable in a war against an adversary with strong air defenses, such as China. They have been used to strike targets inside Iran, according to a March report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).According to the report, PrSM stockpiles were low to start with, since ⁠it is a relatively new munition, but the U.S. military has ordered a large number of them for 2027. The Army has said that ATACMS are being phased out and that production ⁠is shifting to the newer PrSM missiles.Military leaders have for weeks warned the president that stockpiles of defensive weapons — including Patriot interceptors, which are effective against ballistic missiles — were dwindling, said two of ⁠the sources. Last week, several media outlets reported Trump had decided not to launch another massive offensive inside Iran in part because his military advisers had warned about the U.S. stockpile.A U.S. official disputed those accounts, saying Trump chose not to move forward with another attack because of pressure from Gulf states.The Middle East conflict has sparked intense debate about Trump's ​authority to prosecute hostilities against Iran without congressional authorization. No request for a declaration of war or an authorization to ‌use military force has been submitted to Congress.Defensive weapon stocks are also diminished Last week, CSIS published a report estimating that between February and July about 65% of Patriot interceptors had been expended and that the number of THAAD ballistic missile interceptors in U.S. stockpiles was at least 38% lower than at the start of the war. Patriots and THAADs are systems that detect and destroy incoming missiles and are among the most effective in the country's arsenal.While Reuters has not seen the supply figures, those numbers match internal U.S. data, two of the sources said.The U.S. also burned through a little less than half of its global supply of Tomahawk cruise missiles, which are generally launched from ships, since the start of the war, one of the sources said.Reuters could not ​independently verify that number.The Tomahawk is a Navy weapon, launched from destroyers, cruisers and ‌submarines, and has long served as the sea service's principal means of striking heavily defended targets without risking pilots.Raytheon, a unit of RTX, has reached a tentative multi-year agreement with the Pentagon aimed at boosting Tomahawk production, alongside increases in other munitions, as Washington races to rebuild stockpiles.

comments.author: laughing_man
comments.textRawHtml:
>The U.S. Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during its five-month war with Iran, according to three people familiar with the data, raising concerns about the military’s readiness for future conflicts.

>The missiles are principally the Army’s surface-to-surface weapons, known as Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM). The U.S. has used “virtually all” of these weapons, according to two of the sources.

That quite a bit less of an issue than the headline implies.
comments.textZhHtml:
>据三名知情人士透露，美国陆军在与伊朗长达五个月的战争中耗尽了大部分库存的高精度远程导弹，这引发了人们对军队应对未来冲突的准备情况的担忧。

>这些导弹主要是陆军的地对地武器，称为陆军战术导弹系统 (ATACMS) 和精确打击导弹 (PrSM)。据两位消息人士称，美国“几乎使用了所有”这些武器。

这比标题暗示的问题要小得多。

children.author: Maxion
children.textRawHtml: PrSM has been in production for only a short time, and ATACMS stocks were never high. Neither of these are the backbone of US long-range precision strike weapons. Article is misleading.
children.textZhHtml: PrSM 投入生产的时间很短，而且 ATACMS 的库存从来都不是很高。这些都不是美国远程精确打击武器的支柱。文章具有误导性。

children.author: renegade-otter
children.textRawHtml: It IS an issue if stand-off war is your only war, and it seems to be the exclusive approach here. If you run out of long-range precision weapons, what do you have left? Boots on the ground? That's not going to happen, and that means you will never win this on and off war.
children.textZhHtml: 如果对峙战争是你唯一的战争，那就是一个问题，而且这似乎是这里的唯一方法。如果你用完了远程精确武器，你还剩下什么？靴子踩在地上吗？这不会发生，这意味着你永远不会赢得这场战争。

children.author: laughing_man
children.textRawHtml: The USAF has a pretty substantial inventory of stand-off weapons, and an absolutely enormous inventory of guided bombs.
children.textZhHtml: 美国空军拥有相当大量的防区外武器库存，以及绝对庞大的制导炸弹库存。

children.author: renegade-otter
children.textRawHtml: They do, but the current leadership does not have any appetite for entering Iran's airspace after the last downing drama. If Iran captures a pilot, there is going to be no more room for market manipulation.
children.textZhHtml: 他们确实这样做，但在上次击落事件之后，现任领导层没有任何兴趣进入伊朗领空。如果伊朗抓获一名飞行员，那么市场操纵的空间就不再存在。

children.author: theshrike79
children.textRawHtml: Where and who is the pilot who crashed btw?
children.textZhHtml: 顺便说一句，坠机的飞行员在哪里、是谁？

children.textRawHtml:
I doubt the identity of the pilot & WSO will be released -- why would it -- at least not until they retire and write a book about it and out themselves.

children.textZhHtml:
我怀疑飞行员和 WSO 的身份是否会被公开 - 为什么会这样 - 至少要等到他们退休并写一本关于此事的书并自己公布出来为止。

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_F-15E_rescu...

It was big news a few months back.

children.textZhHtml:
几个月前这是个大新闻。

children.author: crote
children.textRawHtml:
But those have to be carried in by planes, and the US doesn't have absolute control over the airspace yet, so that means risking crews.

Is the general public willing to accept downed planes, captured crews, and botched rescue attempts as the new normal?
children.textZhHtml:
但这些必须由飞机运载，而美国尚未完全控制空域，因此这意味着机组人员面临风险。

公众是否愿意接受飞机被击落、机组人员被俘和救援失败成为新常态？

children.author: nixon_why69
children.textRawHtml:
Specific detail, we don't and won't have enough control to do aerial refueling in range of Iran. Tankers aren't stealthy or fast, I'm not sure if they have any countermeasures at all.

One can look at a map of strikes and draw the line on our range, the northeast half of the country is mostly untouched.
children.textZhHtml:
具体细节，我们没有也不会有足够的控制权在伊朗范围内进行空中加油。 油轮不隐秘，速度不快，我不确定他们是否有任何反制措施。

你可以看一下打击地图，在我们的范围内划出一条线，该国的东北半部基本上没有受到影响。

children.textRawHtml: They want this problem to be solved. So you spend the munitions, forcing the manufacturing problem to get fixed. This works in favor of Anduril, which cares about manufacturing scalability
children.textZhHtml: 他们希望这个问题得到解决。所以你花费了弹药，迫使制造问题得到解决。这对关注制造可扩展性的 Anduril 有利

children.author: FuckButtons
children.textRawHtml: Never high and a significant number were donated to ukraine specifically because a ground launched pgm has never been a high priority for the US since the USAF exists.
children.textZhHtml: 向乌克兰捐赠的金额从来不高，而且数量可观，特别是因为自美国空军存在以来，地面发射的PGM从未成为美国的高度优先事项。

children.author: greedo
children.textRawHtml: No PrSM were donated to Ukraine, and only a small number of legacy ATACMS were delivered. Under 200 from open sources...
children.textZhHtml: 没有向乌克兰捐赠任何 PrSM，仅交付了少量旧版 ATACMS。来自开源的不到 200 个...

children.author: throw0101d
children.textRawHtml:
> That quite a bit less of an issue than the headline implies.

Here's a point that I ran across: these long range missiles are there to take out air defences and such (along with stealth sorties), which allows you go go in with 'regular' ordinance and non-stealth aircraft—of which there is much higher quantities and availability—in later phases.

In the early phases of the conflict you use stand-off munitions to reduce the chances of people being captured or killed.

Because Trump doesn't really have approval for this escapade (from either Congress or public opinion) these 'fancy' munitions are the ones primary being used to reduce the risk of casualties.

Now, trying to reduce casualties is not a bad thing per se, but the trade-off is that the fancy stuff is more expensive and takes longer to (re-)build-up. And what if there are other conflicts that flare up where these munitions would be useful? If they're not available do you start using piloted aircraft?
children.textZhHtml:
> 这比标题所暗示的问题要小得多。

这是我遇到的一点：这些远程导弹的目的是摧毁防空系统等（以及隐形飞行），这让你可以在后期阶段使用“常规”法令和非隐形飞机——其数量和可用性要高得多。

在早期阶段在冲突中，你使用防区外弹药来减少人员被俘或被杀的机会。

因为特朗普并没有真正批准这种越轨行为（无论是国会还是公众舆论），这些“花哨”弹药是主要用于减少伤亡风险的。

现在，试图减少伤亡本身并不是一件坏事，但代价是花哨的东西更贵，而且（重新）建立需要更长的时间。如果这些弹药有用的地方爆发其他冲突怎么办？如果没有，您会开始使用有人驾驶的飞机吗？

children.author: FuckButtons
children.textRawHtml: You’re giving trump a lot of credit that you think he’s capable of thinking of second order effects of his actions.
children.textZhHtml: 你对特朗普给予了很大的信任，你认为他有能力考虑他的行为的二阶效应。

children.author: Sabinus
children.textRawHtml: Well I was assured by his supporters that he was a smart and successful businessman and 'very stable genius' so I'm sure this won't end in economic disaster and national humiliation.
children.textZhHtml: 嗯，他的支持者向我保证，他是一位聪明而成功的商人，也是“非常稳定的天才”，所以我确信这不会以经济灾难和国耻告终。

children.author: ocodo
children.textRawHtml:
How could it possibly end in further national humiliation... as long as it's never acknowledged?

I heard the commander in chief is not only acing cognitive tests and winning golf championships, left and right, due to TALENT.

They also are completely vindicated of all accusations, the most powerful man in the history of the world and taken very seriously by some of the stupidest, weakest people to ever exist.

When you have all that going for you and a comfortably filled diaper, what on earth could go wrong!?
children.textZhHtml:
它怎么可能以进一步的国家耻辱告终......只要它从未被承认？

我听说这位总司令不仅在认知测试中取得了优异成绩，并且凭借天赋赢得了左右高尔夫冠军。

他们还完全证明了所有指控都是正确的，他们是世界历史上最有权势的人，并受到一些有史以来最愚蠢、最弱的人的认真对待存在。

当您拥有适合您的一切和舒适的尿布时，到底会出现什么问题！？

children.author: laughing_man
children.textRawHtml:
>Here's a point that I ran across: these long range missiles are there to take out air defences and such (along with stealth sorties), which allows you go go in with 'regular' ordinance and non-stealth aircraft—of which there is much higher quantities and availability—in later phases.

Not ATACMS. SEAD is an Air Force/Navy activity.
children.textZhHtml:
>这是我遇到的一个观点：这些远程导弹的目的是摧毁防空系统等（以及隐形飞行），这样你就可以使用“常规”军令和非隐形飞机——在后期阶段，它们的数量和可用性要高得多。

不是 ATACMS。 SEAD 是一项空军/海军活动。

children.author: greedo
children.textRawHtml: ATACMS and PrSM would definitely be used to strike air defense systems. The US military is very joint and the boundary you're delineating isn't part of the mission tasking.
children.textZhHtml: ATACMS 和 PrSM 肯定会被用来攻击防空系统。美军非常团结，你所划定的边界不属于任务分配的一部分。

children.author: laughing_man
children.textRawHtml: Sure, it's possible in theory.  In reality, the army has other priorities.
children.textZhHtml: 当然，理论上是可能的。  事实上，军队还有其他优先事项。
